description: 4-seed shuffled-context control experiment. Tests whether context-conditioning in the token_diag_core generator provides measurable benefit over a shuffled-context control, or whether the diagonal core advantage is purely a parameter-count effect.
key_findings: Causal core beats shuffled control at r384: 0.4462 vs 0.4491 (diff 0.0029, ~0.6%)
Causal core beats shuffled control at r401: 0.4365 vs 0.4397 (diff 0.0032, ~0.7%)
Shuffled control is close to persistent low-rank at r384: 0.4491 vs 0.4498 (diff 0.0007)
Shuffled control is close to persistent low-rank at r401: 0.4397 vs 0.4405 (diff 0.0008)
Context-conditioning provides a small but consistent measurable benefit
Most of the diagonal core advantage comes from trainable parameters, not context-conditioning
This directly addresses the reviewer requirement for a shuffled-context control
